scope: Per-record JSON batch staging/restoration, quarantine and durable write lifetime

verification.native: 25 targeted tests passed across per-record batches, Domain FIFO/quarantine, routed providers and credential storage. After adding abandoned put/global/backup close regressions, all 14 per-record tests passed in the narrow follow-up.
verification.source: 58 original per-record batch and JSON backend tests passed.

behavior: Validates every key before staging and deduplicates the batch. Documents move to unreadable .deleting paths, then the directory syncs on POSIX before best-effort cleanup. Empty/missing batches create no directories.

Staging or sync failures restore byte-preserved documents and propagate the original error. Failed restoration or restoration sync retains both causes, quarantines later operations and still permits close/reopen.
Tracks each complete batch, record/global write and backup. Abandoning a caller does not cancel accepted writes; close drains them before releasing the backend's open-name slot.

An existing declared table directory remains authoritative even when empty, preventing stale legacy bootstrap after deletion and cold reopen. Compatible numeric stamps admit ordinary JSON numbers but reject booleans.

cleanup.retained: Exact pair/input observations, Source JSON, Native command/log/XML and raw necessary observations; owned files, staged residue and short workspaces removed.

limitations: Finite batch/lifetime/bootstrap contract only; remaining legacy parsing and general filesystem/platform boundaries are not newly certified.
Directory fsync is unsupported and skipped on Windows as in fixed Source. Win7 guest, full regression and release qualification remain pending.
